# Grundlage

Zero-dependency library for building web components with tagged template literals.
Server-rendered and hydrated on the client. `npm install grundlage`.

## Mental model

A component is a generator function passed to `component`. It runs ONCE when the element
mounts and runs to completion (never `while (true)`): setup code runs, you `yield`
something renderable (a render function, an `html` template, or an inner generator), and
the host element is both the first argument and the value every `yield` returns. The
return value is a cleanup function. There are no signals or hooks — re-rendering happens
only when you call `host.update()`. State you declare before the `yield` survives updates
because the yielded render function closes over it; the generator itself does not re-run.

## Complete example

```javascript
import { component, html, props } from "grundlage";

customElements.define(
	"click-counter",
	component(function* (host) {
		const { start } = props(host, { start: [Number, 0] });
		let count = start; // lives in the generator, which runs once — persists across updates

		const increment = () => {
			count += 1;
			host.update(); // re-calls the yielded render function below; count is still here
		};

		yield () => html`<button onClick=${increment}>count: ${count}</button>`;
	}),
);
```

## API

`component(generator, options?) => CustomElementConstructor`
  Register the return value with `customElements.define`. The first argument MUST be a
  generator function (`function*` or `async function*`) — a plain or arrow function
  throws a `TypeError` at definition time, not at mount. `options` extends
  `ShadowRootInit` (default `{ mode: "open" }`); set `formAssociated: true` for form
  components. The generator may be sync or async. `{ mode: "closed" }` hydrates and
  replays `load` data like an open root — the closed shadow root is reached through
  `attachInternals().shadowRoot` instead of `host.shadowRoot`, so server output is reused
  rather than re-rendered.

`` html`...` `` => `Template` (opaque)
  Tagged template literal. Parsed once and cached; later renders only touch dynamic
  parts. Yield it, or embed it inside another `html` template.

`props(host, schema) => typed object`
  Reads typed values whether they arrived as attributes (strings) or properties.
  Schema entry forms: `String` | `Number` | `Boolean` | `Function` | `Array` | a class;
  `[Constructor]` allows `undefined`; `[Constructor, fallback]` supplies a default.
  A present attribute always wins over the property channel: a `Boolean` is `true` when
  the attribute is present, otherwise the own property is read (`el.checked = true`).

`load(host, fetcher, options?) => Promise<Value>`
  Data needed before first render. On the server the fetcher runs and the result is
  serialized into the markup; on the client it's replayed once during hydration, then
  the fetcher runs normally. `options` is `{ key?, skipSsr? }`, or a string shorthand
  for `{ key }`.

Types: `BaseComponent`, `ComponentOptions`, `LoadOptions`, `Template`.

## Bindings

```
content        <p>${text}</p>
attribute      <div class=${className}>
mixed attr     <div class="static ${dynamic}">
event          <button onClick=${handler}>        // on + EventName, camelCase
list           <ul>${items.map((i) => html`<li>${i}</li>`)}</ul>
nested         <div>${show ? html`<details>…</details>` : null}</div>
dynamic tag    <${tagName}>content</${tagName}>
raw            <style>${css}</style>               // style/script/textarea
```

## Host attributes

If the OUTERMOST element of a component's render output is a `<template>`, its attributes
go on the host element and the wrapper is unwrapped (its children become the shadow DOM).
This is how a component sets its own `class`/`id`/`role`/event handlers from the inside.

```javascript
yield () => html`<template class="card" role="${role}" on-form-reset=${reset}>…</template>`;
```

- Static, dynamic, boolean, and multi-part attributes all work and update between renders.
- Spread an object to fan out attributes: `<template ${attributes}>`.
- Event handlers bind here too (e.g. `on-form-*` for form components).
- Attributes dropped by a later render are removed from the host.
- The `<template>` must be top-level — one nested inside content throws.

## Rules — get these right

- The component generator runs ONCE per mount and runs to completion — no `while (true)`.
  State declared before your `yield` persists across re-renders (the yielded render
  function closes over it), so keep mutable state there rather than re-deriving it.
- `host.update()` is the ONLY re-render trigger (no reactive primitive). It re-fires what
  you last yielded: a render function is re-called, a yielded INNER generator restarts
  from scratch, a yielded static `html` template does not re-run. The root never re-runs.
- `await host.update()` resolves when the re-rendered thing has FINISHED: right after paint
  for a template or render function (both synchronous), and — for an async inner generator —
  only once its full run completes, so `await update()` waits for the settled UI, not an
  intermediate frame. A reentrant `update()` called during an in-flight pass coalesces onto
  that pass's promise.
- `yield` returns the host element for a renderable (`html` template, render function, inner
  generator): `const host = yield () => html`…``. A yielded promise returns its resolved
  value (`const data = yield fetch(...)`); any other plain value is echoed back. Yielded
  inner generators and render functions also receive the host as their first argument.
- Components render into SHADOW DOM by default. Light-DOM selectors won't reach inside.
- Don't write literal `<!--^.^ …-->` or `<!--*.*-->` comments in template HTML — those
  prefixes are reserved for internal markers and a collision silently misaligns hydration.
- Events bind in markup as `onEventName=${handler}` (e.g. `onClick`, `onInput`) — not
  `addEventListener` strings and not lowercase `onclick=""`.
- Change detection is HASH-BASED for plain arrays/objects (and Map/Set): mutate-then-
  `update()` we will detect. Other values — class instances, `Date`, typed arrays — are
  compared by REFERENCE identity, so mutating one in place reads as unchanged and is
  skipped. Pass plain data, or replace the reference to signal a change.
- A dynamic `<style>` is fast when every `${…}` sits in a declaration VALUE: the sheet is
  served as static text with `var(--…)` indirection and each value lives as a custom
  property on the HOST's inline `style` (SSR serializes them there too), so an update is a
  `setProperty`, never a sheet reparse. Structural holes (selector, property name, at-rule
  prelude) fall back to a full sheet rewrite — always correct, just slower. Consequences:
  don't deliver a `style` attribute to the host through a `<template ${spread}>` object
  (it wipes those custom properties; a `style` written as a root-`<template>` attribute —
  static or `${…}`-bound — safely disables the fast path for every `<style>` in the
  component, nested templates included), and a value that smuggles `;` or `!important` at
  runtime behaves as invalid → `unset` rather than splitting into extra declarations. A
  CSS-wide keyword (`inherit`/`initial`/`unset`/`revert`) is NOT narrowed — it rides
  through `var()` and takes its normal effect, same as on the fallback path.
- Read inputs with `props(host, schema)`. Don't read attributes directly — they're strings
  and skip the type coercion/defaults `props` gives you.
- `load` replays SSR data on hydration; don't add your own fetch-once cache around it.
- Form components: `component(gen, { formAssociated: true })` exposes `host.internals`
  (`null` on the server) and re-dispatches lifecycle as events `form-associated`,
  `form-disabled`, `form-reset`, `form-state-restore` (or declarative `on-form-*` attrs).
